text:
{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past interactions as continuing demand for broadly related items, with insufficient attention to current purpose and specific fit.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they preserve a specific recurring interest, such as holiday listening, melodic heavy music, fastening supplies, or computer connectivity.",
    "Recommendations also align when they add a useful capability that complements previously acquired equipment."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broadly related items compete with more relevant choices despite serving different tasks, moods, or listening preferences.",
    "Prior purchases are treated as continuing demand even when similar recommendations duplicate capabilities or needs already covered.",
    "Specialized products are recommended without sufficient evidence of compatible equipment, suitable dimensions, or a current use."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Broad category, product-family, era, or collection-format similarity substitutes for a specific reason to choose an item.",
    "Older or isolated interactions appear to carry forward beyond the purpose or occasion that made them relevant."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Recent, repeated behavior receives insufficient weight in distinguishing current tasks and moods from historical interests.",
    "Functional compatibility, incremental usefulness, appropriate quantity, and previously satisfied needs are insufficiently reflected in recommendations.",
    "Specific content connections are often too weak to establish relevance; unidentified items leave fit uncertain rather than demonstrating dislike."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "The top recommendations too often offer broad familiarity without a sufficiently specific, current reason to choose them.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The proportion of top-ranked items users would choose now, distinguished from items they merely consider related or potentially appealing.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to incompatible requirements, redundant capabilities, unsuitable quantities, or absent current needs.",
    "The frequency with which users prefer lower-ranked items because they better match recent tasks or moods.",
    "The frequency of uncertain relevance judgments caused by insufficient identifiable item content, tracked separately from explicit mismatches."
  ]
}
